problem_statement: Build a PWA that replicates the UI/UX and lesson content of the Duolingo Music track so a 7-year-old boy whose access to Duolingo Music is limited can play the full set of music lessons (keyboard playing, games, grading) on his own device.
target_users: The founder's son, a 7-year-old boy who likes Duolingo Music but has limited access (primary user)
The founder/developers, who own and maintain the lesson content (secondary)
core_value_proposition: Give the son unrestricted, self-contained access to a Duolingo-Music-style learning experience — lessons, on-screen piano keyboard, ear training, sight-reading, warmups and scored full-song recitals — that runs offline in the browser with no accounts and no external data sources.

stakeholder_needs.statement: I want a PWA which will replicate the UI and UX of the Duolingo Music track, including all the lessons.
It shouldn't bother with user management.
Persist the data in the browser's local storage.
It should support at least iPhone and iPad.
Use GitHub Actions and deploy in GitHub Pages.
The app shouldn't rely on any external data sources.
The user is my son, a 7 year old boy; he likes Duolingo Music, but his access is limited.
He opens the app and starts the next lesson; it walks him through playing simple tunes with the on-screen keyboard and plays games until the lesson is over, when he is graded for his performance.
The lesson content should derive from the Duolingo Music track (this should be included in the requirements).
GitHub should be used as infrastructure - serving the app, source control and CI/CD; during the operation of the app it should be self contained.
A bit of lagging is fine, but it shouldn't happen too often; since the experience should be mostly offline there's no reason for issues.
Songs should be popular songs - better if unlicensed.
The app should be honest about the results (grading of his performance).
The feedback should be precise on the type of failure.
The app should allow retrying (indefinitely) or switching to another exercise.

in_scope: PWA replicating the UI and UX of the Duolingo Music track, including all the lessons
On-screen piano keyboard: tap, drag, and match keys and notes visually without a physical instrument
Ear training: listen to audio pitches and rhythms, match and identify correct notes
Sight-reading: recognize notes on a musical staff and map them to keyboard geography
Pre-song warmups: low-stakes practice of specific parts or measures of a song before playing it in full
Full song recital: play complete popular songs scored out of 1,000 points on pitch and rhythm accuracy
Star & scoring system: up to three stars per song earned by repeating attempts and improving accuracy
Lesson flow: open app, start next lesson, play tunes on the on-screen keyboard, play games, and be graded at lesson end
Honest, precise feedback about the type of failure when a song is scored poorly
Indefinite retry of a song or switching to another exercise
Persistence of all data in the browser's local storage
Support for at least iPhone and iPad
Deployment via GitHub Actions to GitHub Pages; GitHub used as infrastructure for hosting, source control and CI/CD
out_of_scope: External data sources during app operation — the app is self-contained at runtime
Runtime third-party services such as analytics or a CDN
Licensed Sony Music tracks (popular songs preferred, better if unlicensed)
Robust error handling / recovery experience when a lesson fails to load, progress is lost, or sound does not play (the founder accepts that the son will come to him for aid)
Platforms other than iPhone and iPad
external_integrations: GitHub Pages (static hosting/serving of the app)
None at runtime: the operating app must not consume any external data source or third-party service
constraints: Must be delivered as a Progressive Web App (PWA)

assumption_items.statement: That the game will be enough to keep him entertained in the long run.
Since the experience should be mostly offline there's no reason for issues (lag or sound sync problems).

FOUNDER-DELEGATED: risks - after two interview attempts, the remaining detail is left open for the spec/architecture stage instead of being re-asked. The founder's latest response was: 'That the game will be enough to keep him entertained in the long run.'.

FOUNDER-DELEGATED: glossary - after two interview attempts, the remaining detail is left open for the spec/architecture stage instead of being re-asked. The founder's latest response was: 'A good result would be at least 75% right. The app should be honest about the results.'.

scope_exclusions.item: External data sources while the app is operating (app is self-contained at runtime)
Runtime third-party services such as analytics or a CDN
Licensed Sony Music tracks (popular songs preferred, better if unlicensed)
Robust error-handling / recovery experience for load failures, lost progress or missing sound
Support for platforms beyond iPhone and iPad (e.g. Android, desktop)

done_criteria: On-Screen Piano Keyboard: Tap, drag, and match keys and notes visually without needing a physical instrument.
Ear Training: Listen to audio pitches and rhythms to match and identify correct notes.
Sight-Reading: Learn to recognize notes on a musical staff and map them to keyboard geography.
Pre-Song Warmups: Low-stakes practice environments to learn specific parts or measures of a song before playing it in full.
Full Song Recital: Play complete classical, traditional, or popular tracks scored out of 1,000 points based on pitch and rhythm accuracy.
Star & Scoring System: Earn up to three stars per song by repeating attempts and improving accuracy.
A good result would be at least 75% right.

glossary.Duolingo Music track: the music-learning track in Duolingo whose UI, UX and lessons this app replicates
glossary.lesson: a guided session in which the son plays simple tunes on the on-screen keyboard and plays games, ending with a grade for his performance
glossary.on-screen keyboard: the tappable/draggable piano keyboard that lets keys and notes be matched visually without a physical instrument
glossary.ear training: listening to audio pitches and rhythms and matching/identifying the correct notes
glossary.sight-reading: recognizing notes on a musical staff and mapping them to keyboard geography
glossary.pre-song warmups: low-stakes practice environments to learn specific parts or measures of a song before playing it in full
glossary.full song recital: playing a complete classical, traditional or popular song, scored out of 1,000 points based on pitch and rhythm accuracy
glossary.star & scoring system: up to three stars per song, earned by repeating attempts and improving accuracy
glossary.graded: scored honestly at the end of a lesson or song; at least 75% correct counts as a good result

operational_concepts: When something goes wrong while he's using it - a lesson won't load, his progress gets lost, or the sound doesn't play - he would be very upset and come to me for aid; this is acceptable.
We (the developers) own and maintain the lesson content - the tunes, notes, and game sequences.

research_briefs.brief: Research the unresolved risks question from current authoritative sources and present the method or choice at the review gate.
Research the unresolved glossary question from current authoritative sources and present the method or choice at the review gate.

open_questions: Which single wrong assumption would kill the whole project — the founder does not know (turn 13-14)
Whether the game will be enough to keep the son entertained in the long run (turn 15-16)
What 'laggy' or 'sound out of sync' tolerances actually mean in practice — 'not too often' is unquantified (turn 11-12)
What, concretely, should happen for the son when a lesson won't load, progress is lost, or sound doesn't play — currently 'he comes to me, this is acceptable' (turn 9-10)

Legal/IP provenance of lesson content: it should derive from the Duolingo Music track, and songs should be popular and preferably unlicensed — the source of that content is unspecified (turn 5-6, 19-20)
Lag/stutter frequency threshold that would be considered a defect
